sections.h2: What is Carroll County, Kentucky, and how does it affect a home sale?
sections.html:
Carroll County is a small river county where the Kentucky River meets the Ohio, and its seat, Carrollton, sits at that confluence. At 128.68 square miles of land it is the third-smallest county in Kentucky by area, and the 2020 Census counted 10,810 residents. Carrollton lies about 54 miles from Cincinnati and 55 from Louisville along U.S. 42, with Interstate 71 about four miles south of town.

That location shapes who buys here. The county's own website lists employers such as North American Stainless, CertainTeed and Kentucky Utilities, and describes General Butler State Resort Park, a 791-acre park, as a local draw. Jefferson Community College serves the county. A house in Carrollton is often sold to a worker commuting along the river or I-71 corridor, and Carrollton itself was laid out in 1792 under the name Port William.

Carrollton's worst recorded flood was the Ohio River flood of 1937, with a crest of 79.9 feet, according to Wikipedia. Sellers of low-lying homes near the river should ask the city planning office for floodplain information.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects Carroll County property tax?
sections.html:
The Property Valuation Administrator assesses the property, the Sheriff's Office collects the bill, and the County Clerk handles delinquent real estate taxes. The county's web page describes the clerk's duties as including collection of delinquent real estate taxes, recording deeds and mortgages, and filing wills and probate orders.

  • Sheriff: 440 Main Street, first floor of the courthouse, Carrollton, (502) 732-7010. Online tax search and payments run from the sheriff's page.
  • County Clerk: 440 Main Street, (502) 732-7005, for delinquent taxes and deeds.
  • County administration: (502) 732-5448, which edits or exonerates county tax amounts if a bill is wrong.

The county's FAQ says property taxes are due each year by December 31 and that bills should arrive in October or November. If you did not get one, search the sheriff's page for your bill instead of waiting. Under the state's description, collections start October 1 or November 1 in most counties. Ask the sheriff's office for the exact discount cutoff on a current bill.

sections.h2: Does Carroll County offer a payment plan or waive late fees?
sections.html:
No. The county's FAQ says taxes must be paid in full in a single transaction, and there is no payment plan. It also says that not receiving a bill is not an allowed reason to waive late fees under the Kentucky Administrative Regulations on waivers.

You may combine tender types, for example part check and part cash or card. The penalty structure comes from KRS 134.015:

  • Paid in full by the discount date: 2% off the bill.
  • Through December 31: the amount shown on the bill.
  • January: 5% penalty on tax due and unpaid.
  • After January 31: 10% penalty.

An unpaid bill also continues to a lien. If you sell a Carrollton house with a past-due bill, the buyer's title company will find it, so have the clerk's payoff amount ready.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Carroll County taxes?
sections.html:
The sheriff transfers unpaid bills to the County Clerk after April 15, and a tax sale follows at least 90 days later. KRS 134.128, summarized on the Department of Revenue's collection page, sets the sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, with notices to the owner at 30 and 60 days.

Carroll County held its sale of the 2025 delinquent taxes on July 24, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. in the second-floor courtroom at 440 Main Street, and third-party purchasers had to register by July 14, 2026. The clerk's page lists the clerk's office at (502) 732-7005 for tax sale questions. The state says a third-party purchaser who buys a certificate can charge substantial added fees, so an owner is better off paying before the sale.

If a certificate is paid within five business days of reaching the clerk, the state's example adds interest, a clerk commission and a recording fee, which on a $1,000 bill totals about $1,388. Later payment costs more as the county attorney's commission, postage and advertising fees accrue.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Carroll County assessment?
sections.html:
Request a conference with the PVA, then file with the county clerk's office after the roll closes. Carroll's tax roll is open for 13 days from the first Monday in May, and the appeal must follow a conference with the PVA or a deputy, per the state calendar.

The state tells owners the PVA must send a notice if it raises a value above what you listed. A buyer's deed price can also count as the listed value for the next January 1 assessment if the property was not changed. For a Carroll County seller who bought recently, that means the purchase price may be the PVA's starting point, so keep your closing statement.

If the local board decreases or increases a value, it must explain why in writing, and you may record the hearing. Do not skip the board if you want any further review, because failing to file or appear ends your right to go on.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Carroll County owners claim?
sections.html:
Owners 65 or older, and owners who are totally disabled, can claim the homestead exemption on a primary residence. The Department of Revenue says Form 62A350 serves both the age and disability exemptions, and the PVA keeps the form on file.

The exemption removes a fixed dollar amount from the assessed value, not the whole value, and the amount is adjusted every two years. It does not transfer to a buyer. Veterans with a total service-connected disability need file only once, and so do owners found disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement System.

Ask the PVA for the current dollar amount, because the dollar figure published on the state's page covers a past assessment period. A seller who is 65 should confirm the exemption was applied before closing.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Carroll County?
sections.html:
Carroll County's median owner-occupied home value is $140,900 in the 2020 to 2024 Census estimates, between Caldwell's $118,500 and Calloway's $183,200. Only 65.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, second-lowest among the four counties in this series, and the 2025 population estimate of 11,141 is up 3.1 percent since 2020.

The Census counted a single building permit in Carroll County in 2025, so most buyers are choosing among existing homes. Sellers who cannot wait for financing, or who are managing an estate or a rental with tenants, can sell as-is for cash and pay the tax payoff from the proceeds.

faqs.q: When is Carroll County property tax due?
faqs.a: All property taxes are due by December 31 each year, and a discount applies to bills paid by the early cutoff on your bill. January adds a 5% penalty and later payment adds 10%.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan in Carroll County?
faqs.a: No. The county says taxes must be paid in full in one transaction, though you can combine check, cash and card.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about delinquent taxes in Carroll County?
faqs.a: Call the County Clerk at (502) 732-7005. The clerk collects delinquent real estate taxes and runs the tax sale.

faqs.q: Will Carroll County waive a late fee if I never got my bill?
faqs.a: No. The county's FAQ says not receiving a bill is not a permitted reason to waive late fees. Search your bill on the sheriff's page in October or November.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Carrollton house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer can purchase as-is, and the tax payoff is paid from your proceeds at closing. Get the payoff from the County Clerk before you sign.
